First, an overview... In the Go game there are only two types
of moves, urgent moves or large moves. An urgent move means you
must help your stone or group become settled or comfortable (or
punish your opponent's stone or group that is not settled or
uncomfortable). You can see if something is uncomfortable by
imagining enemy stones coming close to it with effect. If no
urgent move is required, then take the largest move. (Go is so
simple, eh?)

So let's see. Is the F3 stone uncomfortable? Of course it is.
It has a liberty and a connection problem. BUT ! ... (there is
always a but)

Is F3 an important stone? We can tell this way. If a stone secures
something, connects something, or cuts the enemy, it is important.

any of those things. If the stone is unimportant, then helping
it can not be urgent...   Perhaps Black needs to tenuki (play elsewhere) and take the largest

and reduces the white zone (has double purpose).

Ok, a battle ending. We take a look at it.
You said" Not Unhappy...." Now we change our aspect. When it helped B to settle down, whether we can think Black are helping White to build territory and thickness group?!

In Go world, there are some keys that is like the axiom and theorem in our world. One of the most important keys is the relation of thickness and weakness. You game is showing us what thickness group is and what weakness group is.
M3 is weakness group.
N5 group is thickness group.
P11 group is thickness group.
R14 group is weakness group.
R7 group is thickness group but NOT useful.
Why say so? Here is explaination.
M3 is weakness group relative to thickness group N5. This thickness affect M3's life and promise that right-bottom corner is white's territory.
According same reason, R14 group is weakness group relative to P11 group. So if white move R17, black will lose basement and in danger.
R7 group is thick, correct! But NOT useful. This group is closed by white and can't affect outside. It can't help M3 group or any other groups. Just protect its limited territory. Only 11 points.

Our conclusion is that pay attention thickness and weakness when playing. Thickness group will affect very much and sometimes make weakness group in danger.

Either way, there are much bigger plays available than L19 and L17.

Comment: Now a very important point:

You
have spotted that this move is an atari, and the stones that you are
putting into atari are very important cutting stones, so if you play
atari, white has to answer at A.   OK, so you can play this atari at
any point, white has to answer, and you know exactly what answer you
are going to get.   On the other hand, the only way for white to stop
you playing this atari, is to play some slow gote move. This is not
going to happen in the middle of a fight like this. So, what is even
more important is that you don't to play this atari yet.

Why should you wait? Well, to start with there might be a ko later, and this would be a brilliant ko threat.

Another
reason is that once you have played the atari, your opponent knows
exactly what is going on. If you don't play it yet, your opponent has
to worry about the possibility that you could play it at any time.

Also,
there is not just this atari. You can also play atari at A, which would
be equally forcing. Are you sure that you won't want to play A any time
in the future?

And as for making the opponent worry, if you
don't play the atari, your opponent has to worry about both this move
and A all the time.

Also, after this atari followed by white A,
white is very thick at the top. The chances are that you have actually
helped white here.

So, in summary, a forcing move like this
gives you the right to play on a particular point in sente; nut, more
importantly, it gives you the right to not play the move (and keep it
in reserve) as well.   When you understand this fully, you will find
that you get a lot stronger at fighting.

The book "Beyond Forcing Moves" (one of my favourite Go books) is all about this.
